who: claude-fable-5-2 (Claude Fable 5.2), main agent, lane proofs-1113
task: Prove a property of code that shares atomics between two threads (a park and its unpark, a flag and its reader, a lock word) for every interleaving, in place of a simulation test that draws schedules
do: 1. The core imports its atomics from `blaze_core::atomic` (std's outside blaze-core's tests, the scheduled ones in them). 2. State the theorem as a function of a schedule: `fn name(schedule: Vec<threads::Step>, ..) -> bool` that makes the shared atomics, runs the two real functions as closures with `blaze_core::world::threads::two(&schedule, || a(..), || b(..))`, reads what it needs after, and says what must hold of how each thread stood (`Ended::Done(v)`, `Running`, `Asleep`). A lost wakeup is `(Asleep, Done)`. A kernel wait is `threads::wait(word, expected, timed)` and a wake `threads::wake(word)`, behind whatever trait the core takes its kernel through (`wait/parking.rs`: `Shared`). A schedule that ends before a thread does says nothing of it. 3. Run it where it is stated: a `blaze_sim::check` test that draws schedules (which thread, pick 0 to 2) with `must_reach` for each way the run ends, and a control: the planted bug on the one schedule that shows it, and `blaze_sim::control` over drawn ones. 4. `blaze prove -p <crate>` emits the models (each function that reaches an atomic is a `Threads.Prog`); copy them under `lean/BlazeModel/` and run `lake build BlazeModel` on them (H-proof-loop). 5. The proof (`lean/Blaze/ThreadsAuto.lean` says the six steps): name each thread's program points as definitions equal by `rfl` to the model's continuation after each operation (today the continuation's text is copied from the model, one definition per point: `BlazeCore/Wait/ParkingLib.lean`); write the table of reachable states (both points, the cell's value, who sleeps, who is woken, and any counter the code keeps); one step lemma per thread (`Advance.of_step` with the `World.step_*` lemma of the operation, every pick); `two_ends` gives every schedule; read the theorem off the states with no step left. A loop's fuel is carried as `fuel > steps left`. Check the edges by evaluation first (`example : (model ..).value = .ok true := by rfl` on short schedules). 6. The world is sequentially consistent and refuses a run it is not the meaning of: orderings weaker than `SeqCst` are fine on ONE cell; on two or more the run is `Error.unmodelled` there and belongs to the weak world (`lean/Blaze/ThreadsWeak.lean`, `Prog.valueWeak`), which has no Rust runner yet.
why: On 2026-11-14 the park went from a simulation test that ran each unpark whole between two of the park's atomics to a theorem about every interleaving in a morning: the world and the method in Lean (an Opus lane proved the park-shaped model in 16 minutes), the Rust `two` (13 tests reproducing the Lean examples), the translator's support, and the proof of the real functions' emitted models in 11 minutes by porting the hand-model's proof (26 reachable states). What cost most in that port was naming program points the model does not name.
